strategy_title: Autotuning num_warps/num_stages without tile size changes regresses
strategy_description: Adding @triton.autotune that only varies num_warps and num_stages while keeping tile sizes (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K) fixed caused a 24% regression (55 us → 69 us). The winning config selected a smaller block size (64 threads vs 128), which increased registers per thread from 128 to 168, reduced theoretical occupancy from 25% to 18.75%, and cut waves/SM from 0.18 to 0.12 — the opposite of the intended effect. When the root bottleneck is insufficient grid coverage and low occupancy due to large tile sizes, autotuning only num_warps/num_stages cannot fix it and may make it worse by selecting configs that spill more registers.
applicable_when: Kernel has very low waves/SM (<0.5) and low achieved occupancy (<10%) due to large fixed tile sizes; the plan calls for autotuning to increase grid coverage.
do_not_apply_when: Tile sizes are already small or the bottleneck is not grid coverage; autotuning only num_warps/num_stages when tile sizes are the root cause of low occupancy will not help and may regress by selecting configs with higher register pressure.
framework_notes: In Triton, @triton.autotune configs must include the tile-size constexprs (BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K) as dict keys if those are the parameters driving grid size and register pressure. Configs with empty dicts {} only vary num_warps/num_stages and cannot change the grid shape or register allocation driven by tile sizes.

The kernel uses tl.dot with BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=32 tiles. Triton stages A and B tiles through shared memory before feeding them to the MMA unit. With BLOCK_K=32 floats (128 bytes = 32 banks x 4 bytes), consecutive threads in a warp access the same bank when the shared memory stride is a multiple of 128 bytes. Changing BLOCK_K to 40 makes the shared memory row stride 160 bytes (160 mod 128 = 32), breaking the alignment and eliminating the 12-way conflict. TF32 was already tried and failed correctness (item 99ce2458). Autotuning num_warps/stages only also regressed (item exp_iter1_autotune_num_warps_stages_only). The fix must include tile sizes as autotune dict keys so the grid lambda can adapt.

applicable_when: The kernel is severely underutilized: only 0.18 waves/SM and 6.25% achieved occupancy. The root cause is that BLOCK_M=64, BLOCK_N=64, BLOCK_K=32 are hardcoded as tl.constexpr inside the kernel body, so the @triton.autotune configs (which only vary num_warps/num_stages via empty dicts {}) cannot change tile sizes, register pressure, or grid coverage. With 128 registers/thread and 32KB shared memory per block (64*64*4*2 bytes for A+B tiles), only 4 blocks fit per SM, and the 93-block grid covers only 0.7 SM-waves, leaving 39 SMs completely idle. The fix is to promote BLOCK_M, BLOCK_N, BLOCK_K to kernel parameters (tl.constexpr arguments) driven by autotune configs, AND update the grid lambda to compute cdiv(M, BLOCK_M) * cdiv(N, BLOCK_N) dynamically. Smaller tiles (e.g., 32x32) reduce the accumulator from 64*64=4096 to 32*32=1024 floats, cutting register pressure and allowing more blocks/SM. A 32x32 tile grid would have ceil(1960/32)*ceil(192/32)=62*6=372 blocks, 4x more coverage. Prior attempts that changed tile sizes failed correctness (max_diff~100) because the grid remained static at (93,1,1) while tile sizes changed, causing wrong-tile accumulation. This plan fixes both simultaneously. TF32 is excluded (correctness failure). Autotune-num_warps-only is excluded (24% regression).
